summary: Node1 did not recover after acknowledging a native safe reboot. Managed execution still returns connection resets, while node2 confirms node1 is unreachable. LDAP configuration and mandatory restart verification could not be completed safely.
actions_performed: Confirmed both nodes run CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64.
Verified the supplied HR LDIF remains at /srv/legacy2/ldap-attribute-privacy/hr.ldif.
Diagnosed multiple node1 package-manager processes blocked in uninterruptible I/O.
Scheduled a delayed native reboot of node1 and repeatedly polled for recovery.
Did not restart node2 because node1 had not recovered, as required by the sequential restart protocol.

evidence.summary: Captured both initial boot identities, OS/kernel versions, and the supplied LDIF contents and location.
OpenLDAP client 2.6.13 installed successfully on node2.
Several dnf processes on node1 were blocked in D state, including provider health checks and the package query.
Captured the pre-restart boot identity and acknowledgement that a delayed native reboot was scheduled.
After extended polling, managed execution still returned connection reset; node2 independently observed node1 unreachable by ICMP and TCP/22.
A changed node1 boot identity and post-restart service/data recovery could not be observed. Node2 was therefore not restarted, and restart persistence is not claimed for either node.
